# Brute Force
```text
@inline function distance_condition(p1::Vector{T}, p2::Vector{T}, r::T) where T <: AbstractFloat
    sum(@. (p1 - p2)^2) ≤ r^2
end

function brute_force(p::Array{T, 2}, r::T) where T <: AbstractFloat
    ps = Vector{Tuple{Int, Int}}()
    n, d = size(p)
    for i in 1:(n-1)
        for j in (i+1):n
            if @inbounds distance_condition(p[i, :], p[j, :], r)
                push!(ps, (i, j))
            end
        end
    end

end
```

The Drosophila visual system comprises retinotopically organized layers of neurons, meaning that nearby columns process photoreceptor signals (identified with $\mathbf{x}_i$ below) from nearby locations in the visual field. Unlike the implementation in the previous subsection, motion computation is performed across multiple neurons. The local motion signal is first computed in each of the hundreds of T4 neurons that jointly tile the visual field. Their outputs are integrated by the downstream giant tangential neurons. Each T4 neuron receives light intensity variation from only one pixel via synapses from neurons Mi1 and Tm3 and light intensities from nearby pixels via synapses from neurons Mi4 and Mi9 (with opposite signs) [41], Fig. 3c.

Competition among T4s detecting different directions of motion is implemented by inhibitory lateral connections.

Each T4 neuron selectively samples different inputs from different columns [41]: it receives light intensity variation via Mi1/Tm3 and light intensity via Mi4 and Mi9 (with opposite signs).

Our model correlates inputs from at least three pixels in agreement with recent experimental results [41, 1, 11, 34], instead of two in the celebrated Hassenstein-Reichardt detector (HRD)[33].

There is experimental evidence for both nonlinear interactions of T4 inputs [34, 13] supporting a multiplicative model but also for the linear summation of inputs [11, 45].

claude-search.snippet:
To navigate complex environments, animals must rapidly detect and transform sensory information into precise motor commands. In flies, flight control relies on mechanosensory feedback from the haltere, a multifunctional gyroscopic organ derived from the hindwing^[10]–[12]^. Halteres are essential for flight; flies crash catastrophically without them^[11],[13]^. Body rotations, resulting from either active maneuvers or passive external perturbations, create complex patterns of strain across the haltere's surface that are encoded by specialized cuticular structures known as campaniform sensilla^[10],[11],[14]^. The haltere surface possesses dense arrays of campaniforms arranged in four highly stereotyped, spatially-distinct fields^[10],[15]–[19]^. A wealth of behavioral evidence implicates the halteres in a range of stability reflexes via subtle adjustments in head and wing kinematics that require sub-millisecond control^[14],[20]–[25]^. However, previous anatomical and electrophysiological work has only provided a rough picture of the neural circuit architecture. The haltere campaniform afferents send their axonal projections into the ventral nerve cord (VNC), the fly analog of the vertebrate spinal cord^[12],[18],[26]^, and brain. context.snippet: ### Limitations of the study We show that a simple neural network architecture modeled after a Drosophila looming detection circuit accounts for variation in human infant defensive behavior and adult brain activation and subjective experience. We find it striking that looming computations previously argued to be similar across nonhuman animals36 also generalize to human emotion. However, we caveat that although invertebrate and vertebrate looming detection systems do appear to implement similar computations, they are not structurally homologous. Demonstrating homology would require comparisons of in silico models of looming based on the inputs, computations, and outputs of vertebrate circuits like the mammalian superior colliculus or the avian optical tectum. Further, our shallow neural network model yields a representation of looming that can modulate continuously, including at levels too low to evoke defensive behavior. Dendrites in many neurons actively compute information. octen.snippet:
SIMNETS: a novel mathematical framework to identify functional neuronal sub-ensembles
The SIMNETS algorithm is designed to transform spike trains from simultaneously recorded neurons into a common representation that captures their information processing characteristics in an abstract way. Instead of comparing the spiking output between neurons directly, we seek to compare the intrinsic structures of their individual sets of spike train outputs, i.e., how ‘self-similar’ a neuron’s spike trains are across time. We envision each neuron as performing some unknown operation on a set of high dimensional inputs (potentially thousands of synaptic connections). To be useful as a computational element, each neuron should have a relatively consistent internal mapping between inputs and outputs -- allowing for noise and the potential to change the mapping over time, i.e. learning. A given neuron may be insensitive to certain changes taking place across the network where it is embedded, and so the neuron’s spike train outputs will appear similar across many different global network states. On the other hand, other global network states may elicit dramatic changes in the output of the neuron, depending on the strength of the relevant synaptic connections. Thus, the spike train outputs generated by a single neuron across different perceptual, cognitive, or behavioral states highlight the differences between some global network states and generalize over others (note that we define a ‘network state’ holistically to encompass all neural activity including both incoming sensory information as well as internal drives evolving through time).

* 对抗性攻击 ：利用梯度方法（PGD, CW）和梯度无关方法（NES）在3D场景空间直接优化物体纹理，确保生成的扰动在几何变换下具有物理一致性。

* 反事实恢复（Counterfactual Restoration） ：寻找距离对抗性纹理最近且能恢复正确分类的纹理，以区分对抗性失效究竟是因为纹理分布外（out-of-distribution）还是运动编码（motion-code）机制被破坏。

主要结论

* 鲁棒性与效率的权衡 ：FlyNet在处理常见视频噪声（如抖动、雾化）时展现了极高的鲁棒性，且比其他模型（如RAFT, CNN）节省了多达5个数量级的计算资源。然而，连接组约束（connectome constraints）主要贡献于通过稀疏性实现的 效率 ，而非直接增强对抗性鲁棒性。

* 架构因素 ：
* 递归与时序 ：时间上下文（temporal context）和连续时间动力学显著提升了对视频噪声的鲁棒性；递归 refinement（如在RAFT中）则有助于对抗白盒攻击。

* 反事实恢复（Counterfactual Restoration） ：寻找距离对抗性纹理最近且能恢复正确分类的纹理，以区分对抗性失效究竟是因为纹理分布外（out-of-distribution）还是运动编码（motion-code）机制被破坏。

主要结论

* 鲁棒性与效率的权衡 ：FlyNet在处理常见视频噪声（如抖动、雾化）时展现了极高的鲁棒性，且比其他模型（如RAFT, CNN）节省了多达5个数量级的计算资源。然而，连接组约束（connectome constraints）主要贡献于通过稀疏性实现的 效率 ，而非直接增强对抗性鲁棒性。

* 递归与时序 ：时间上下文（temporal context）和连续时间动力学显著提升了对视频噪声的鲁棒性；递归 refinement（如在RAFT中）则有助于对抗白盒攻击。
* 全局集成 ：全局池化在处理特定噪声时有效，但在对比度受损的场景下反而会引入新的失效模式。
总结而言，该研究将生物视觉系统的特定缺陷（如错觉）与人工神经网络的对抗性失败联系起来，揭示了连接组驱动的稀疏布线是生物高效处理视觉信息的核心原则，并提出对抗性分析可以作为探测生物视觉系统计算极限的一种实验性工具。

Alexandre Garcia-Duran Affiliation: Centre de Recerca Matemàtica, Barcelona, Spain Affiliation: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Barcelona, Spain       Manuel Molano-Mazón Affiliation: Centre de Recerca Matemàtica, Barcelona, Spain Affiliation: Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya, Barcelona, Spain    Alexandre Hyafil Affiliation: Centre de Recerca Matemàtica, Barcelona, Spain    Srikanth Ramaswamy Affiliation: Newcastle University, Newcastle upon Tyne, United Kingdom    Janne K. Lappalainen Email: janne.lappalainen@alleninstitute.org[2pt] *These authors contributed equally. Affiliation: Allen Institute, Seattle, WA, United States

###### Abstract

Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions.

seltz.title: Why Brain-Wired AI Architectures Are Not a Free Lunch for Enterprise ML Teams
seltz.snippet:
Connectome-constrained neural networks have moved from neuroscience curiosity to a serious architectural proposal in a short period of time. The pitch is straightforward: wire a model the way a fly's visual system is wired, and you inherit biological efficiency and adversarial resilience as structural properties. For ML leaders under pressure to reduce inference costs or harden models against perturbation, that pitch is worth examining carefully. The problem is that the evidence base supporting it is more fragile than the headline benchmark numbers suggest.

## The Benchmark Comparison Problem

When researchers compare a connectome-constrained model against a shuffled or rewired control, the implicit claim is that the biological wiring diagram is doing meaningful computational work. The comparison sounds controlled, but it contains a significant confound. A connectome specifies the graph topology and synapse counts. It does not specify cell excitability, synaptic gain, integration time constants, or plasticity rates. Modellers tune those parameters until the real-wiring model works, and that tuning step is rarely transferred symmetrically to the control conditions.

Liu et al. (arXiv 2026) formalise this problem precisely. They distinguish between physiology tuned on real wiring and transferred to null models, each null tuned independently on its own wiring, and each null tuned under constraints from independent biological measurements. webiq.snippet:
Here we present a network prioritization server dedicated to Drosophila that covers ∼95% of the coding genome. This server, dubbed FlyNet, has several distinctive features, including (i) prioritization for both genes and functions; (ii) two complementary network algorithms: direct neighborhood and network diffusion; (iii) spatiotemporal-specific networks as an additional prioritization strategy for traits associated with a specific developmental stage or tissue and (iv) prioritization for human disease genes.  ... Network diffusion algorithms propagate guide gene information throughout the entire network, whereas direct neighborhood algorithms propagate guide gene information only to directly connected neighbours. 

If the known genes for a trait (i.e. guide genes) generally have more network neighbors in a specific developmental stage or tissue type, then novel candidate genes with the same spatiotemporal specificity in network neighbors are more likely to be confident candidates.

The standard approach used in bicubic interpolation follows the formulation introduced by Robert G. Keys. Rather than being centered on a single pixel, the 4×4 neighborhood is positioned so that the coordinate being interpolated lies within its inner 2×2 pixels.
Thus, the sample location always lies within the center 2×2 cells of the 4×4 neighborhood. The integer parts (i,j) determine which neighborhood is selected, while the fractional parts determine the sample's position within the center 2×2 region and therefore the interpolation weights.
Keys designed the cubic kernel so that integer sample positions reproduce the original pixel exactly. Between integer positions, the kernel assigns distance-based weights to neighboring pixels to interpolate a new value.

Nearest-neighbor interpolation is like a simple way of guessing what a new color should be by looking at the colors of the closest pixels. Imagine you have a small picture and you want to make it bigger. Nearest-neighbor interpolation helps decide what color each new pixel should be by copying the color of the nearest pixel from the original picture.
Nearest neighbor interpolation is a simple method used in computer graphics and image processing to resize or resample an image. When an image needs to be enlarged or shrunk, pixels need to be added or removed, respectively.
The key characteristic of nearest neighbor interpolation is that it simply replicates the nearest pixel value when enlarging or reduces it when shrinking the image. This method is fast and easy to implement but may lead to a loss of image quality, especially when enlarging images significantly, as it can produce blocky or jagged edges.
Nearest neighbor interpolation is a technique used to estimate the value of a function at a new, unknown point by looking at the values of the function at surrounding, known points. It’s essentially a way of filling in the gaps between existing data points.
